title: Preparing for a general clinic visit
preparation_items: Write down your main symptom or concern in one or two sentences, including when it started and whether it's getting better, worse, or staying the same.
List any medicines you are currently taking, including the dose if you know it.
Bring a valid ID and, if you have one, your hospital or clinic card or folder number.
Bring any past test results, scan reports, or prescriptions related to this visit.
Write down any questions you want to ask, so you don't forget them once you're with the health worker.
Arrive early if you can — some clinics see patients in the order they arrive, not strictly by appointment time.
variability_note: Exactly what's needed can vary by clinic — always confirm requirements with the facility directly before you go.

title: Preparing for an antenatal appointment
preparation_items: Bring your antenatal card or maternal health record if you already have one — if this is your first visit, bring your ID instead.
Note your last menstrual period date, if known, and how many weeks pregnant you believe you are.
List any symptoms you've noticed — swelling, headaches, vision changes, unusual pain — even mild ones, so the health worker can check them.
List any medicines or supplements you are currently taking.
Bring results of any earlier pregnancy scans or lab tests, if you have them.
Write down any questions about your pregnancy, diet, or upcoming appointments.
variability_note: Antenatal schedules and required tests vary by facility and by stage of pregnancy — always confirm with your antenatal clinic directly.

title: Preparing for a postnatal appointment
preparation_items: Bring your maternal and newborn health record or antenatal card if you have one.
Note how many days or weeks after delivery this visit is, and how the delivery went (vaginal or caesarean, any complications).
Note anything you want checked for yourself — bleeding, pain, mood, feeding difficulties — and for the baby — feeding, weight, jaundice, umbilical cord healing.
Bring the baby's newborn/vaccination card if one was already started.
Write down any questions about recovery, breastfeeding, or contraception.
variability_note: The exact postnatal check-up schedule and what's checked at each visit can vary by facility — always confirm with your clinic directly.

title: Preparing to take a child for vaccination
preparation_items: Bring the child's immunization/vaccination card — this is the most important thing to bring, so the clinic can record what's given and know what's due.
If this is the first vaccination, bring the child's birth record and your own ID.
Note the child's current weight and age if you know them, and mention any recent illness, fever, or allergic reaction to a past vaccine.
Dress the child in clothing that makes it easy to access the arm or thigh.
It's normal for a child to be fussy after a vaccine — ask the health worker what reactions are expected and what would need a follow-up visit.
variability_note: Vaccination schedules and available vaccines can vary by facility and by programme — always confirm the current schedule with your clinic directly.

title: Preparing for an adult vaccination visit
preparation_items: Bring your ID and, if you have one, a record of vaccines you've previously received.
Mention any current illness, fever, pregnancy, or known allergies — especially any past allergic reaction to a vaccine.
List any medicines you're currently taking, particularly anything affecting your immune system.
Ask which vaccine you're receiving and what side effects are normal versus what would need follow-up care.
variability_note: Which vaccines are recommended or available can vary by facility, age, and health status — always confirm with your clinic directly.

title: Preparing for a laboratory test
preparation_items: Ask in advance whether the specific test requires fasting (not eating or drinking, other than water, for a number of hours beforehand) — this varies by test.
Bring the lab request form or referral note from your health worker, if you were given one.
Bring your ID and any previous results for the same test, so changes over time can be compared.
Mention any medicines or supplements you're taking, since some can affect certain results.
Wear clothing that makes it easy to access your arm if the test needs a blood sample.
variability_note: Preparation requirements (especially fasting) differ a lot by the specific test — always confirm with the laboratory or the health worker who ordered it before your appointment.

title: Preparing for an imaging appointment (X-ray, ultrasound, scan)
preparation_items: Bring the referral or request form from your health worker.
Ask in advance if the specific scan needs preparation — some ultrasounds need a full bladder, some scans need fasting, and this varies by scan type.
Tell the facility if you are, or might be, pregnant before any X-ray or CT scan.
Wear clothing without metal (zips, buttons, jewellery) if you can, since some scans require removing metal objects.
Bring any previous scan images or reports for comparison, if you have them.
variability_note: Preparation needed is very specific to the type of scan — always confirm directly with the imaging facility before your appointment.

title: Preparing for a dental appointment
preparation_items: Note when your tooth or mouth problem started, and describe the pain or issue as specifically as you can.
List any medicines you're taking and any allergies, especially to local anaesthetic or antibiotics.
Mention any conditions like diabetes, heart problems, or pregnancy, since these can affect dental treatment.
Eat a light meal beforehand if you can, especially if you expect a procedure — ask the clinic if fasting is needed for your specific treatment.
Bring your ID and any previous dental records if you have them.
variability_note: What's needed can vary depending on the specific dental procedure — always confirm with the dental clinic directly.

title: Preparing for a chronic disease follow-up appointment
preparation_items: Bring your ongoing medical record, folder, or care card for this condition.
List all medicines you're currently taking for this and any other condition, including doses if you know them.
If you monitor anything at home (blood pressure, blood sugar, weight), bring your recent readings or a log of them.
Note any new or worsening symptoms since your last visit, and anything that's made your condition harder to manage.
Write down questions about your treatment plan, side effects, or lifestyle changes.
variability_note: What's tracked and reviewed depends on your specific condition and care plan — always confirm with your regular health worker directly.

title: Preparing for a specialist consultation
preparation_items: Bring the referral letter from the health worker who referred you, if you have one.
Bring your full medical history related to this issue, including past test results, scans, and prescriptions.
List all medicines you're currently taking.
Write a short summary of your main concern, when it started, and what treatments you've already tried.
Write down your questions in advance, since specialist appointments can be short and focused.
variability_note: What a specialist needs can vary a lot by specialty — always confirm with the referring health worker or the specialist's clinic directly.
